errors.english: I, the preceptor named [note: insert preceptor name here], shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here]
errors.why: The speaker is the officiating bhikṣu (las byed pa); the instrumental mkhan mo ... bas qualifies the candidate ('N, whose preceptress is N'), it does not identify the questioner as the preceptress.

fix.find: I, the preceptor named [note: insert preceptor name here], shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here]
fix.replace: I shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here], whose preceptress is the woman named [note: insert preceptor name here],

errors.english: This is the time for your emergence.
errors.why: 'byung ba'i dus renders bhūtakāla, 'the time for what is actually the case (facts)', paired with 'the time for truth', not 'emergence'.

errors.english: Are you not a runaway?
errors.why: brkus pa means 'stolen/abducted', not a runaway.

errors.english: Are you not a debtor?
errors.why: rtsod pa can means a person under dispute (a contested person in litigation), not a debtor.

note: Readable rendering of the bhikṣuṇī ordination formula, but the questioner is misidentified as the preceptress and several items in the list of impediments are mistranslated.

errors.english: the phrases "repeatedly desiring," "to whatever small extent," and "all" are established as the rule
errors.why: yang dang yang du 'dod pa can qualifies the words 'however little' and 'all' (they carry the sense 'again and again'); it is not a separate phrase 'repeatedly desiring'.

errors.english: there is nothing more to it than what was previously shown to others
errors.why: gzhan la here means 'otherwise': the reason given is that otherwise the rule would add nothing beyond what was already taught.

note: Sound rendering of the commentary on the weaving rule; a couple of glossing phrases in the commentator's argument are misconstrued.

errors.english: a contradiction with a treatise that one has accepted as a peer
errors.why: mtshungs means the contradiction with a treatise is equivalent to (the same as) contradiction with what one has accepted; nothing about accepting it 'as a peer'.

errors.english: why is it necessarily based only on what the opponent has accepted?
errors.why: The cited root text poses the question and answers it ('because it is necessarily only what that party has accepted'); the English turns the answer into a question.

note: Generally faithful handling of the pramāṇa discussion of thesis faults, with two slips in the argument about contradiction with a treatise.
Faithful rendering of the ten masteries, the three things not needing guarding, and the marks of the great man.

errors.english: this reality never becomes an object of perception
errors.why: de refers to the saṃbhogakāya under discussion (seen only by those on the bhūmis), not to 'reality'.

errors.english: The first two exist conventionally
errors.why: btags pa'i yod is 'imputed/designated existence' (prajñaptisat), which the commentary goes on to explain (on what they are imputed); 'conventionally' blurs the term.

note: Good translation of the trikāya passage, with a referent slip and a softened technical term.

errors.english: he saw a hunter wearing a garment marked with the color of a golden swan in the forest
errors.why: The prince looks at his own garment marked with golden swans and wishes for forest garb; the hunter only appears in the next verse.

fix.find: he saw a hunter wearing a garment marked with the color of a golden swan in the forest. Being steadfast, he felt a desire for those clothes.
fix.replace: in the forest he looked at his own garment marked with golden swans, and the steadfast one longed for garments fit for the forest.

errors.english: possessing the body of a blue deer
errors.why: ri dwags sngon/rngon pa is a deer-hunter (Skt. mṛgavyādha): the deity takes the form of a hunter, who speaks as 'the hunter' below.

fix.find: possessing the body of a blue deer [note: original: (mriga) deer or forest animal]
fix.replace: in the body of a deer-hunter

errors.english: if you have no attachment to peace in this place
errors.why: zhi ba is a vocative ('gentle one', Skt. saumya) and 'dir refers to the robe: 'gentle one, if you have no attachment to this'.

fix.find: if you have no attachment to peace in this place
fix.replace: gentle one, if you have no attachment to this robe

errors.english: Having turned back his followers whose faces were wet with tears
errors.why: 'dun pa is the proper name Chanda(ka), the charioteer, whom the prince sends back; not 'followers'.

fix.find: Having turned back his followers whose faces were wet with tears
fix.replace: Having sent back Chanda, whose face was wet with tears

errors.english: as if harvesting the blue petals of a lotus
errors.why: The blue utpala petal describes the drawn sword (dark as a blue lotus petal), not the cutting of the hair.

errors.english: Please take it and wear these white ones.
errors.why: The hunter asks the prince to accept the robe and give him the white garment, which the hunter then takes; he is not offering white clothes.

note: Buddhacarita verses on the renunciation: the narrative is recognisable but the hunter is introduced too early, Chanda becomes 'followers', and several vocatives and similes are misread.

errors.english: To explain the meaning of the gathering:
errors.why: 'dus par bya ba'i phyir closes the preceding sentence: the half-verse is repeated as the fourth 'for the sake of compression'; it does not introduce an explanation of 'the gathering'.

errors.english: From the initial "A" to the final "Ho," these four are
errors.why: The 'four' are the four la syllables between the initial a and the final ho; the English drops 'la' and leaves 'these four' unidentified.

note: Careful word-commentary rendering; two small misconstruals in the explanation of the apabhraṃśa song.

errors.english: From these words that are worth grasping and venerable words, it emerges with certainty in order to exhaust suffering.
errors.why: nas is the list abbreviation 'up to': the list of speech qualities runs on to speech that leads to deliverance (niryāṇa) for ending suffering; nothing 'emerges from' the words.

note: Faithful rendering of the Nāmasaṃgīti commentary on the lord of speech, with one list-abbreviation misread.

errors.english: At the site of the student
errors.why: bdag po'i gnas is the site of the master/lord (as in 'the five masters' just above), not the student.

fix.find: At the site of the student
fix.replace: At the site of the master

errors.english: Alternatively, bind the sky above the eyes of (Vajrabhairava) The Adamantine Terrifier.
errors.why: The sky is bound by means of the Vajrabhairava-eye mudrā (defined just after), not 'above the eyes' of the deity.

note: Competent rendering of the ritual mantras and mudrās; one misidentified site and one mudrā name misread.

errors.english: Once the sign of stability is not found
errors.why: rnyed nas means 'having found': emanation and reabsorption follow once the sign of stability is obtained.

fix.find: Once the sign of stability is not found
fix.replace: Once the sign of stability is found

note: Accurate account of the subtle yogas and the mantra-garland recitation, apart from one inserted negation.
